RISK_INVESTIGATION_ACT1_EMAIL.instructions: A few unread messages are sitting in the project inbox.

questions.answerText:
Team —

Officially underway as of today. Quick summary for anyone catching up: we're standing up a new manufacturing facility for the medicine, with an NHS supply contract riding on hitting first production inside 24 weeks. Budget's £12M, MHRA's given provisional approval so validation is on us to keep moving.

More detail to follow once the PID's finalised.

Good to be working with all of you.
— E

Ellis — wanted to get ahead of this rather than raise it in the room. If cleanroom install slips even two weeks, MHRA validation slips with it, and we lose the buffer to Board's 24-week promise. I don't think anyone's accounted for that risk yet. Can we talk before Thursday?
— Camille

questions.questionText: FW: Isolator delivery — supplier chasing sign-off
questions.answerText:
Ellis — PharmaCraft's chasing again, they need a decision on the isolator spec by Friday or they can't hold the slot. This is the third reminder. Can you or someone confirm which way we're going?
— Tomasz
Steering call moved again — new time TBC. Fourth time this month.
Can we please lock a date. Validation doesn't fix itself.

questions.questionText: Camille Okafor: Can we please lock a date. Validation doesn't fix itself.
questions.answerText: Agreed — can we make this the first item next time, not the last?
Has anyone updated the PID?
Minutes from three months ago. Nobody's touched them since.
Old versions, half of them named "FINAL_v2_reallyfinal."
The kickoff deck. The objectives slide still has placeholder text on it.
A budget tracker. Half the formulas reference a tab that isn't there anymore.
Three risks logged, all from month one. Nothing added since.

RISK_INVESTIGATION_CONTRACTOR.instructions: Pick 2 of these 3 questions to ask Vaughn.

questions.questionText: How reliable have they been so far?
questions.answerText: They've missed two calls in two weeks. That's not like them.

questions.questionText: What happens if they don't show up in time?
questions.answerText: We lose three weeks minimum, maybe more.

questions.questionText: Is there a backup option if this falls through?
questions.answerText: Not one we've qualified yet — but I know a firm that might work.

RISK_INVESTIGATION_VALIDATION.instructions: Pick 2 of these 3 questions to ask Camille.

questions.questionText: How likely is this to actually slip?
questions.answerText: If nothing changes upstream, close to certain.

questions.questionText: What does a slip actually cost us?
questions.answerText: Every week here pushes the MHRA inspection back the same amount.

questions.questionText: Is there any way to buffer this without extending the whole schedule?
questions.answerText: We could run validation in parallel on the lower-risk steps. It's tight, but possible.

RISK_INVESTIGATION_CONTINGENCY.instructions: Pick 2 of these 3 questions to ask Daniel.

questions.questionText: How likely are we to actually need more than what's budgeted?
questions.answerText: Given how this project's gone so far? I'd bet on it.

questions.questionText: What happens if the contingency runs out?
questions.answerText: I freeze spending. Everything stops, including things that shouldn't.

questions.questionText: Is there anywhere else in the budget we could pull from if it comes to that?
questions.answerText: There's slack in the training line. Not much. But some.
